An 8-digit number with nondecreasing digits has all digits in 1..9 (first digit nonzero forces all ≥1), and is determined by its multiset of digits. Subtracting 1 from each digit gives a partition of 40−8=32 into at most 8 parts, each ≤8, i.e. the coefficient of q^32 in the Gaussian binomial [16,8]_q (partitions fitting in an 8×8 box).

Using [16,8] = [15,7] + q^8[15,8] = (1+q^8)[15,7] and the symmetry of [15,7] (degree 56), the count is c32+c24 of [15,7] = 2·c24([15,7]) = 2·Q(24,7,8), where Q(n,k,m) = # partitions of n into ≤k parts each ≤m.

Q(24,7,8) by number a of parts equal to 8:
- a=3: remainder 0 → 1
- a=2: remainder 8 into ≤5 parts each ≤7: p(8)=22 minus part '8' (1) minus partitions with ≥6 parts (4) → 17
- a=1: remainder 16 into ≤6 parts each ≤7: p_6(16)=136 minus those with largest part ≥8 (18+13+10+7+5+3+2+1+1=60) → 76
- a=0: remainder 24 into ≤7 parts each ≤7: p_7(24)=733 minus those with largest part ≥8 (L=8:94, 9:91, 10:83, 11:69, 12:58, 13:44, 14:35, 15:26, 16:20, 17:14, 18:11, 19:7, 20:5, 21:3, 22:2, 23:1, 24:1; total 564) → 169

Here p_k(n) tables (partitions into parts ≤k) computed via p_k(n)=p_{k-1}(n)+p_k(n−k): p_6(11..16)=44,58,71,90,110,136; p_7(24)=733.

Q(24,7,8) = 1+17+76+169 = 263, so the answer is 2·263 = 526 (matching the known central coefficient of [16,8]_q).
